description:
Canonical identity is separate from OIDC token. One person can authenticate via multiple IdPs (LF SSO, GitHub, Google) and reach the same mailboxes.

Schema:
  identities(identity_id PK, email, display_name, active bool, created_at, updated_at)
  identity_providers(identity_id FK, issuer, sub, trust_level, linked_at, linked_by, PRIMARY KEY (issuer, sub))

trust_level values: managed | verified | federated
  managed: foundation-controlled IdP (LF SSO/Okta), SCIM-provisioned, high trust
  verified: third-party with verified email (GitHub, Google), medium trust
  federated: any OIDC provider, low trust

Auto-linking rules:
  managed→managed: auto-link on matching foundation-issued email, safe
  verified→managed: auto-link only if email is foundation-issued on both sides
  verified→verified: require user-confirmed or admin linking, not auto

linked_by values: scim | auto-email | admin | user-confirmed

Login flow:
  token arrives with issuer + sub
  → look up identity_providers WHERE issuer=? AND sub=?
  → found: get identity_id, check active, proceed
  → not found: attempt email linkage per trust rules above
  → still not found: create new identity + provider record

OIDC provider config gains trust_level field:
  [[auth.oidc_providers]]
  issuer = "https://sso.linuxfoundation.org"
  trust_level = "managed"
  scim_enabled = true

  [[auth.oidc_providers]]
  issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  trust_level = "verified"
  scim_enabled = false

min_trust_level on mailboxes: session must have an active provider at or above this level to access the mailbox. If not, stoa returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate pointing at a required managed IdP (step-up auth). The client re-authenticates and the session gains a second active provider.
notes:
DoD/GSA door-open decision: add 'hardware' as a fourth trust tier above 'managed'. Maps to PIV/CAC smart card authentication (client certificate with Federal Common Policy CA chain). trust_level values in order: hardware > managed > verified > federated. hardware tier slots PIV support in cleanly when needed without restructuring the access control model. PIV is client cert auth with specific CA chain — stoa-reader already has client_certs skeleton. Keep that path from rotting. Also note: every access control decision must write an audit log row (grant check, token validation, SCIM event, mailbox access) — government auditors need 'who accessed what when' for any message any time. Gaps are findings.
Identity ID format decision: UUIDv7. Time-ordered, good B-tree index locality, RFC 9562, no external coordination, not derived from any IdP attribute so stable across provider changes and merges.

DID support: future, not v1. Users will be able to add DIDs to their identity later as an additional credential type, same linking ceremony as IdP providers. Schema placeholder:

  CREATE TABLE identity_dids (
      identity_id  TEXT NOT NULL,  -- UUIDv7
      did          TEXT NOT NULL,  -- did:key:z6Mk... or did:web:... etc
      linked_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
      linked_by    TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'user-confirmed' | 'admin'
      PRIMARY KEY (did)
  );

DID method priority when implemented: did:key first (self-contained, no external resolution), then did:web, then others explicitly. did:ion and blockchain-dependent methods last.

Long-term payoff: cross-instance stoa federation. Two stoa instances both recognizing did:key:z6Mk... means same person authenticates to both without central registry or manual linking. Do not design anything now that forecloses this.
title: design: identity model — identities, providers, trust tiers
